Title: New Application for Registering for an USI course

If you want to register for a course at the sports institute, you need to select a course.
If slots are free, the system tells you the courses, and dates.
Select one.
Next, you need to check if you already have an account at the sports institute.
If not, you need to check whether you are registered at an eligible university.
If you are, register your account.
If you are not, request an activation and wait for a response.
As soon as you have an account, log into it.
The application is also connected to your twitter account, and lets you tweet to friends who might want to join you, you can complete the registration for the course and provide the payment information.
In the end, you will receive a course ticket.

result.rule: When the description states that an activity's result or a condition determines which of multiple alternative paths follows: Connect the activity to an exclusive gateway and model each alternative as a separate outgoing branch.

When the description says that one or more of several optional actions may be selected, including that multiple actions may be performed together: Model the alternatives with an inclusive gateway so any nonempty combination of the actions can proceed.

When the description states that a participant checks whether a completion condition has been met before the process can proceed: Model the check as a distinct activity performed by that participant, followed by a decision gateway whose condition routes the flow back to the relevant earlier steps or onward when the condition is met.

result.rule: Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
When the description does not justify a specialized construct, use the simplest compatible BPMN construct and do not guess missing semantics.
Do not merge separately described actions into one task or split one stated action without a process reason. Preserve described dependencies.
Represent each modeled internal workflow with bpmn:process. Use isExecutable=false unless execution-ready behavior is explicitly required and fully specified.
Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.

Follow the BPMN XML schema: never put a documentation element directly inside bpmn:definitions, and never nest a sequenceFlow inside a task, gateway or event. If you add an ioSpecification, it must contain its dataInput and dataOutput elements first, then at least one inputSet and one outputSet, even if empty: <bpmn:inputSet/><bpmn:outputSet/>.
